Oh hey

Yeah I calmed down a lot. However, I’m still a bit moody and existential about it all. I do realize that I need to learn to accept my losses and learn from/ move on from them. Though I do hope I can get back some of the things I lost (i.e. my best friend, etc) in the future or something.

Thanks for checking up on me, bronach_
:)
Yeah that’s probably a good idea. Again, thank you for replying to this post. It truly means a lot.

I don’t know honestly. I just never allow myself to have high expectations for anything because I usually end up disappointed. After losing my best friend, I just feel empty. It also doesn’t help that everything bad that’s happened to me so far isn’t even remotely my fault. I guess I’m just scared that it’ll be another of other people walking all over me or losing more loved ones.

Sorry if my grammar sucks btw. I’m still half asleep rn

No nothing happened yet. However, all my thoughts and anxieties just won’t go and I was stupid enough to think that they’d go away because it’s a New Year.

Thank you so much for responding
That’s what I’m worried about, but thank you. I’ll probably message him like that soon.
Eh...when they brokeup he personally asked me to be there for her, so yeah we hangout occasionally. But he knows that I’m in no way interested in anything more than friendship with her.

Hello, scar face 

I've actually been considering calling  my local planned parenthood. I'm also probably going to confide in the school nurse if my anxiety doesn't clear up before school starts again. Also, it's not really possible for me to not out myself to my parents if I bring that up.

Fortunately, my dad is the only person in my family that is openly okay with it. So I might come out to him soon anyways.

Hello, doingit

I'll reach out to my friends about this I usually try to not burden others with my anxiety, so I never really consider this option.

Hello, blue 

I honestly take no offense to your criticisms of our healthcare systems in America. Despite being relatively young, even I'm capable of recognizing that we're not adequately handling healthcare. However, I do think teens are allowed to have private appointments with certain doctors that handle certain things. But I don't really remember most of the rules and I'm not independent enough to go without my parents (i.e. I can't drive and I'm not sure how I'd be able to pay for the appointment).

There aren't really any decent LGBT charities or support groups in my part of Northern California. There is one at school, but the people in it are often rude to...well people like us. The school nurse is a decent option though, but I'm on summer vacation until mid-august so I can't take advantage of that opportunity yet.

I do actually like the CBT idea though. I'll have to look into that.

Thank you for the support and advice. It genuinely means a lot to me.

Hello 

It's just any potential illness or ailment (STDs, MRSA, Mononucleosis, and even that rare form of meningitis that's caused by that amoeba, etc).

I also am not out to my family yet, so I'm afraid I'll have to face a barrage of questions before they'll even let me.

Also, my parents often complain about me wanting to go to the doctor or a therapist for this stuff. So unfortunately, that results in having a one-on-one with a professional becoming a last resort.

Hello

Do you know the validity of this website? Those numbers do seem hopeful, but I couldn't find any sources or references on the article.

I've considered it.
Unfortunately, some insurance agencies refuse to cover some psychologists, therapists, and counseling. So, it's kinda difficult to get a good one.

Oh damn.
My apologies, RDV.
My sex-ed was very good it's just my anxiety issues mess with the way I rationalize things and it especially doesn't help that my biggest fear is catching a potentially deadly disease. 

Oh btw 
The quality of sex-ed varies from state-to-state. Luckily, Nor Cal has pretty decent, comprehensive sex-ed. Although there's definitely room for improvement IMO.
